questions.question: A cystic lesion located in the 'anterolateral' wall of the upper vagina, above the level of the pubococcygeus muscle, is likely a:
questions.detail: Gartner duct cysts are embryologic remnants of the Wolffian duct.

questions.question: Which cystic lesion is located 'periurethral' and can cause urethral obstruction or recurrent infections?
questions.detail: These are the female homologues of the prostate and are located at the urethral meatus.

questions.question: A 'Bartholin gland cyst' is characteristically located:
choices: At the level of or below the pubococcygeus muscle, in the posterior vaginal wall
questions.detail: These are located in the superficial perineal pouch.

questions.question: A 'saddle-bag' configuration of a fluid collection surrounding the urethra is diagnostic of:
questions.detail: This out-pouching often wraps around the urethra.

questions.question: 'Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser (MRKH) syndrome' is characterized by:
choices: Mullerian duct aplasia (absent uterus and upper 2/3 of vagina)
questions.detail: Patients have normal ovaries but congenital absence of the uterus and vagina.

questions.question: Which imaging modality is 'first-line' for characterizing suspected Mullerian duct anomalies?
questions.detail: 3D ultrasound and MRI are both excellent for distinguishing septate from bicornuate uteri.

questions.question: 'Hematocolpos' refers to:
choices: Blood-filled vagina, typically due to an imperforate hymen
A malignant tumor of the vagina
questions.detail: This presents in adolescent girls who have not yet begun menstruating despite cyclic pain.

questions.question: A 'grape-like' mass in the vagina of a young girl is the classic presentation of:
questions.detail: This is a rare but highly characteristic pediatric vaginal malignancy.
